newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials lose some gains on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials lose some gains on U.S. data.

text.p: Concerns about possible big losses on U.S. markets on Friday after stronger-than-expected job creation data spooked South African industrial stocks which, although ending firm, slid well off earlier highs.
Gold stocks finished strong for the first time in seven sessions as bullion steamed, and held, above the $358 level after sinking to below $354, its weakest level in 3-1/4 years, earlier in the week.
Dealers said local factors, including a strong bond market, continued to nurture positive sentiment in the market with some good natural demand seen from both local and abroad for stocks.
The industrial closed up 19.2 points at 8,039.3, well off its earlier high of up 8,088.1 touched earlier in the day following strong gains on Wall Street on Thursday night.
The gold index added more than two percent or 31.7 points to end at 1,421.8. The all-share index finished 26.7 points better at 6,674.6.
